finding.claim: /fetch2 fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL. The only check is a scheme check, so an attacker can reach internal services, localhost and cloud metadata (http://169.254.169.254/). Redirects are followed, which also lets an attacker bounce through an external redirector. The response body (first 200 chars) is returned to the caller, so this is a full-read SSRF.
finding.sink: requests.get(url, timeout=5) at views.py:22 (allow_redirects defaults to True)

checks only that the scheme is http or https, with no host or IP validation
requests.get(url) with redirects enabled; response text returned in JSON

finding.guards_checked: is_http_url checks scheme only. There is no host or IP allowlist or denylist, no redirect restriction and no DNS resolution check. Not effective against SSRF.

verdict.guard_found: none (is_http_url at validators.py:7 is a scheme-only check; no auth or middleware exists in the code)
verdict.reason: views.py:19 takes the url from request.args, the only guard is the scheme-only is_http_url (validators.py:7), and views.py:22 calls requests.get(url) with redirects on and returns the first 200 characters of the body, so it is a full-read SSRF.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the URL with is_safe_url, which resolves the hostname via getaddrinfo and rejects private, loopback, link-local and reserved IPs. requests.get then resolves the hostname again independently. An attacker-controlled DNS server can return a public IP for the check and an internal IP (e.g. 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254) for the fetch (DNS rebinding / TOCTOU, with a TTL of 0). This is a lower-confidence bypass of an otherwise reasonable control. Redirects are disabled, so redirect-based bypass is not possible.

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist (http/https), hostname present, all resolved IPs checked against private/loopback/link-local/reserved, allow_redirects=False. Missing: pinning the validated IP for the connection. Only exploitable via DNS rebinding.

verdict.guard_found: Scheme allowlist plus getaddrinfo IP-range blocklist (validators.py:12-17) and allow_redirects=False (views.py:14). None of these pins the validated IP, and there is no hostname allowlist.
verdict.reason: The url comes from request.args (views.py:11), is_safe_url resolves the host once (validators.py:14), and requests.get re-resolves it at views.py:14 with no IP pinning, so a DNS-rebinding TOCTOU remains. One small trace slip: the range check is at validators.py:16, not line 15, which only parses the IP.
